title: [CLO Beginner's Guide] Quick Start Tutorial
description: CLO Beginner's Guide - Quick Start Edition, CLO technical experts take you through a comprehensive introduction to the CLO interface and basic operations, solidifying your learning foundation.

Try the fabric properties

the physical properties

real fabric draping

However,

Animation complete simulation mode  
Use it when making animations.  
Additionally,  
at the bottom of the menu,  
you can choose

GPU simulation maintains  
the same simulation accuracy  
but with faster speed than CPU simulation.  
Therefore,  
GPU simulation mode is recommended.  
Switch to GPU simulation.  
You can see that  
the simulation icon changes  
from a 10-star arrow  
to a grounded air star arrow.  
Press Control + G to start simulation.  
The icon turns blue.  
Press Control + G again  
to stop simulation,  
and it turns gray.  
This helps us identify  
the current simulation mode  
and calculation engine.  
Finally, let's look at the  
simulation mode.  
This is the GPU simulation mode.  
In this simulation mode,  
the resulting resolution  
may be approximately 0.6 ARE  
or 2500 px.  
The simulation mode  
reflects the simulation quality.  
If the simulation mode  
is set to 0,  
the simulation module  
can be read as 0.6  
or 300 px.  
However, when switching the simulation mode,

Clothing

The front side of the 3D clothing shows the real fabric,

You can distinguish the fabric’s front and back,

Find the file menu in the left corner, save the project file, and set the file name in the pop-up window.  
At the same time,  
note that the file format we save is ZPRJ, which is the most commonly used project file format in CLO.  
The file will contain 3D clothing, virtual models, rendering attribute settings, animation information, and other data such as colors.  
In addition, common CLO formats also include ZPAC clothing files,

chunks.content: ## CLO Software Interface Overview This section covers the main interface components and terminology of CLO software, including the 3D and 2D windows, toolbars, menus, and library system, essential for navigating and managing virtual clothing design. When you open CLO software, the interface features two main windows side by side: the **3D window** on the left and the **2D window** on the right. - **3D Window:** Used for simulating virtual clothing with 360-degree viewing and adjusting garment shapes. - **2D Window:** Used for creating, editing, and sewing patterns. Above the 2D window, there is a vertical menu bar controlling display options for information within the window. Both sides of these windows have corresponding toolbars—the **3D toolbar** and the **2D toolbar**—which provide tools specific to each window's functions. The **top menu bar** includes options to create, open, import, and export projects or clothing files. The **Edit menu** offers common operations like undo, redo, copy, and paste. There is a dedicated **3D menu** for 3D-related functions and a **2D design menu** for pattern-related tools. Language settings and user-defined controls can be found here as well. The **user-defined window** allows customization of Try Control keys (mouse buttons) and software units, appearance, toolbar positions, and version display. The reset button restores the default interface layout if the screen becomes disordered. ## CLO Account and AI Studio Features This section explains account identification, AI Studio functions, and resource management options, key for enhancing design realism and accessing CLO assets. On the top right, your **account ID** appears in blue text beside a pink **CLO AI Studio** icon. CLO AI Studio offers AI-powered features such as face changing and voiceover to create realistic 3D clothing images. First-time users should activate AI functions via the tutorial guide. Next to this is the **library button** (blue icon), which opens the library window for managing CLO materials. The library includes: - **Default CLO Library:** Contains pre-installed clothing, models, fabrics, accessories, and scene materials. - **CLOSET Platform:** A cloud resource platform accessible through the CLOSET tab for digital assets. - **CONNECT Tab:** Access to a public mall for purchasing and downloading additional resources. - **My Library:** You can create a personal library by adding local material files, facilitating quick access. Materials can be previewed in icon or list view. Items with a small square icon indicate they are not downloaded; you can download them via the dedicated button. Virtual models come with multiple options (e.g., Luna, a female youth model, and adult models). Model configuration, posture, and size can be adjusted. Right-clicking a material allows copying its local path or opening the folder in the resource manager. ## Working with Virtual Models and Materials This section details how to load, position, and manage virtual models and materials, fundamental for garment fitting and design. To load a virtual model, open the virtual model folder, select a model (female models are categorized by age), and add it to the work area by double-clicking, dragging, or right-clicking and confirming the add action.

chunks.content: Right-clicking a material allows copying its local path or opening the folder in the resource manager. ## Working with Virtual Models and Materials This section details how to load, position, and manage virtual models and materials, fundamental for garment fitting and design. To load a virtual model, open the virtual model folder, select a model (female models are categorized by age), and add it to the work area by double-clicking, dragging, or right-clicking and confirming the add action. When adding, you can choose to open size and position options in the garment. If multiple model files exist, you can trace their folder paths or navigate using file layers. Downloaded materials and models can be managed through the resource manager, with easy access to local file locations. ## Interface Layout and Window Controls This section explains layout management and window display options to optimize workspace efficiency. At the bottom of the window: - The **bottom left** displays the software version number. - The **bottom right** contains layout control buttons allowing toggling between: - Default state (both 3D and 2D windows visible) - 3D only - 2D only - Reset button to restore default layout ## Try Control and Mouse Settings This section describes the Try Control mouse button assignments and basic 3D/2D navigation controls, important for manipulating the workspace efficiently. Due to system differences, Try Control buttons vary between Windows and Mac; this guide uses default Windows settings. - **Middle mouse wheel:** Press and hold to pan vertically. - **Right mouse button:** Hold and drag to rotate the 3D view. - **Scroll wheel:** Zooms in and out. In the 3D window, clicking an object centers rotation around that point, enabling 360-degree inspection. Fixed-angle views can be accessed by holding the right mouse button in the background and selecting presets or using numeric keypad shortcuts: - Position 5: model's location - Position 2: front view - Positions 4 and 6: side views The 2D window supports zoom and pan but does not allow rotation (since it is a flat plane). Right-clicking a blank area in either window selects all objects proportionally within the view. Pressing **F** centers the selected object (panels, models, or garments) in the window. ## Selection Tools in 3D and 2D Windows This section details how to select and manipulate garment panels and pieces across 3D and 2D views, ensuring synchronized editing. - Use **Select Move Tool (shortcut Q)** in the 3D toolbar to select and move garment pieces. - Selected pieces highlight yellow in both 3D and corresponding 2D windows. - Click an empty area to deselect. - Double-click or Shift + double-click selects linked sewing groups. - Use **Ctrl + A** to select all. In the 2D window: - Use **Adjust Panel Tool (shortcut A)** to select and adjust panel edges. - Selections are highlighted yellow, consistent with the 3D window. - You can create a selection frame by left-clicking and dragging over panels. - Partial selection can be added by holding Ctrl while dragging.

chunks.content: - Click an empty area to deselect. - Double-click or Shift + double-click selects linked sewing groups. - Use **Ctrl + A** to select all. In the 2D window: - Use **Adjust Panel Tool (shortcut A)** to select and adjust panel edges. - Selections are highlighted yellow, consistent with the 3D window. - You can create a selection frame by left-clicking and dragging over panels. - Partial selection can be added by holding Ctrl while dragging. - Irregular selection frames can be drawn by double-clicking to start, clicking points to define the polygon, and returning to the start point to complete. - Ctrl can be used to add panels within irregular selections. ## Loading and Positioning Garments on Models This section explains how to import garments, align them with virtual models, and use positioning tools for accurate fitting. Open a female model, right-click, and add it to the work area, selecting the option to open size and position in the garment. If the garment and model do not align, use the **Select Move Tool** in the 3D window to move the garment. - Double-click a panel to select all connected panels by sewing. - Drag to move the entire garment. Because movement occurs in 3D space but mouse input is 2D, controlling garment movement can be challenging. Using the **Positioning Ball Tool** is recommended for precise adjustment. The positioning ball consists of: - Three straight axes (translation along X, Y, Z) - Three arcs (rotation) - A square between straight lines (translation within a plane) There are three positioning ball coordinate modes: 1. **Screen Coordinates:** Axes rotate with the camera perspective (default). 2. **World Coordinates:** Fixed 3D axes independent of camera and object orientation. 3. **Local (Horizontal) Coordinates:** Axes follow the object’s orientation, useful for adjusting model joints or movements. Switch coordinate modes by right-clicking in the 3D blank space. Use shortcuts (e.g., 2 for front view, 4/6 for side views) to help position the garment correctly on the model. Ensure the entire garment is selected during movement, or only the selected panel will move. The 2D window’s Adjust Panel Tool can also move panels without affecting the 3D garment’s position. ## Simulation Modes and Fabric Behavior This section covers the fabric simulation process, different simulation modes, and hardware acceleration options, which are critical for realistic garment fitting. Start simulation by clicking the first tool in the upper left or pressing **Control + G**. During simulation: - The 3D window displays fabric draping with physics-based behavior. - The mouse cursor changes to a small grip tool, allowing garment shape adjustments via click-and-drag. There are three simulation modes: 1. **Normal Speed (Default):** Accurate physical simulation of fabric properties; recommended for garment creation and fabric behavior observation. 2. **Animation Complete:** Used for animating garments. 3. (Third mode not explicitly named in the transcript, implied as varied simulation quality.) Simulation engine can run on: - **CPU:** Standard processing speed. - **GPU:** Faster simulation with equal accuracy; recommended for performance.

There is a dedicated **3D menu** for 3D-related functions and a **2D design menu** for pattern-related tools. Language settings and user-defined controls can be found here as well. The **user-defined window** allows customization of Try Control keys (mouse buttons) and software units, appearance, toolbar positions, and version display. The reset button restores the default interface layout if the screen becomes disordered. ## CLO Account and AI Studio Features This section explains account identification, AI Studio functions, and resource management options, key for enhancing design realism and accessing CLO assets. On the top right, your **account ID** appears in blue text beside a pink **CLO AI Studio** icon. CLO AI Studio offers AI-powered features such as face changing and voiceover to create realistic 3D clothing images. First-time users should activate AI functions via the tutorial guide. Next to this is the **library button** (blue icon), which opens the library window for managing CLO materials. The library includes: - **Default CLO Library:** Contains pre-installed clothing, models, fabrics, accessories, and scene materials. - **CLOSET Platform:** A cloud resource platform accessible through the CLOSET tab for digital assets. - **CONNECT Tab:** Access to a public mall for purchasing and downloading additional resources. - **My Library:** You can create a personal library by adding local material files, facilitating quick access. Materials can be previewed in icon or list view. Items with a small square icon indicate they are not downloaded; you can download them via the dedicated button. Virtual models come with multiple options (e.g., Luna, a female youth model, and adult models). Model configuration, posture, and size can be adjusted. Right-clicking a material allows copying its local path or opening the folder in the resource manager. ## Working with Virtual Models and Materials This section details how to load, position, and manage virtual models and materials, fundamental for garment fitting and design. To load a virtual model, open the virtual model folder, select a model (female models are categorized by age), and add it to the work area by double-clicking, dragging, or right-clicking and confirming the add action. When adding, you can choose to open size and position options in the garment. If multiple model files exist, you can trace their folder paths or navigate using file layers. Downloaded materials and models can be managed through the resource manager, with easy access to local file locations. ## Interface Layout and Window Controls This section explains layout management and window display options to optimize workspace efficiency. At the bottom of the window: - The **bottom left** displays the software version number. - The **bottom right** contains layout control buttons allowing toggling between: - Default state (both 3D and 2D windows visible) - 3D only - 2D only - Reset button to restore default layout ## Try Control and Mouse Settings This section describes the Try Control mouse button assignments and basic 3D/2D navigation controls, important for manipulating the workspace efficiently. Due to system differences, Try Control buttons vary between Windows and Mac; this guide uses default Windows settings. - **Middle mouse wheel:** Press and hold to pan vertically. - **Right mouse button:** Hold and drag to rotate the 3D view. - **Scroll wheel:** Zooms in and out. In the 3D window, clicking an object centers rotation around that point, enabling 360-degree inspection. Fixed-angle views can be accessed by holding the right mouse button in the background and selecting presets or using numeric keypad shortcuts: - Position 5: model's location - Position 2: front view - Positions 4 and 6: side views The 2D window supports zoom and pan but does not allow rotation (since it is a flat plane). Right-clicking a blank area in either window selects all objects proportionally within the view. Pressing **F** centers the selected object (panels, models, or garments) in the window. ## Selection Tools in 3D and 2D Windows This section details how to select and manipulate garment panels and pieces across 3D and 2D views, ensuring synchronized editing. - Use **Select Move Tool (shortcut Q)** in the 3D toolbar to select and move garment pieces. - Selected pieces highlight yellow in both 3D and corresponding 2D windows. - Click an empty area to deselect. - Double-click or Shift + double-click selects linked sewing groups. - Use **Ctrl + A** to select all. In the 2D window: - Use **Adjust Panel Tool (shortcut A)** to select and adjust panel edges. - Selections are highlighted yellow, consistent with the 3D window. - You can create a selection frame by left-clicking and dragging over panels. - Partial selection can be added by holding Ctrl while dragging. - Irregular selection frames can be drawn by double-clicking to start, clicking points to define the polygon, and returning to the start point to complete. - Ctrl can be used to add panels within irregular selections. ## Loading and Positioning Garments on Models This section explains how to import garments, align them with virtual models, and use positioning tools for accurate fitting. Open a female model, right-click, and add it to the work area, selecting the option to open size and position in the garment. If the garment and model do not align, use the **Select Move Tool** in the 3D window to move the garment. - Double-click a panel to select all connected panels by sewing. - Drag to move the entire garment. Because movement occurs in 3D space but mouse input is 2D, controlling garment movement can be challenging. Using the **Positioning Ball Tool** is recommended for precise adjustment. The positioning ball consists of: - Three straight axes (translation along X, Y, Z) - Three arcs (rotation) - A square between straight lines (translation within a plane) There are three positioning ball coordinate modes: 1. **Screen Coordinates:** Axes rotate with the camera perspective (default). 2. **World Coordinates:** Fixed 3D axes independent of camera and object orientation. 3. **Local (Horizontal) Coordinates:** Axes follow the object’s orientation, useful for adjusting model joints or movements. Switch coordinate modes by right-clicking in the 3D blank space. Use shortcuts (e.g., 2 for front view, 4/6 for side views) to help position the garment correctly on the model. Ensure the entire garment is selected during movement, or only the selected panel will move. The 2D window’s Adjust Panel Tool can also move panels without affecting the 3D garment’s position. ## Simulation Modes and Fabric Behavior This section covers the fabric simulation process, different simulation modes, and hardware acceleration options, which are critical for realistic garment fitting.
